title: PAVXploreRL: Physical-Action-Visual World Model Reinforcement Learning with Action Exploration; submitted: 2026-07-18; categories: cs.CV; authors: Han Wang; Zijun Wang; Shuoshuo Xue; Rui Cao; Fengjiao Chen; Xiaodan Liang; Roy Ka-Wei Lee; abstract: Action-conditioned world models are a key component of embodied AI, serving as scalable policy evaluators that reduce reliance on expensive real-world rollouts. To accurately capture diverse action-induced dynamics, such models should satisfy three key objectives-Physical Plausibility (P), Action Adherence (A), and Visual Fidelity (V), collectively referred to as PAV-while remaining robust to both in-distribution (ID) expert demonstrations and out-of-distribution (OOD) actions. However, existing methods primarily rely on ID action-video pairs and pixel-level reconstruction losses, which do not explicitly optimize PAV objectives and generalize poorly beyond expert data. To address this, we propose PAVXploreRL, a reinforcement learning framework built on a pretrained latent world model that explicitly optimizes PAV objectives through reward-driven training.
